rationale: Add a test that enforces the `#[non_exhaustive]` attribute on `SearchResults` (`crates/trust-but-verify/src/sources/public.rs#struct[SearchResults]`). For example, add a `compile_fail,E0639` doctest on the struct, like the one on `outline::Span`, that builds `trust_but_verify::sources::SearchResults { matches: vec![1], complete: true }` from outside the crate. Mark it with {test}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.SearchResults`. — The subject's declaration requires `#[non_exhaustive] pub struct SearchResults<T>`, which constrains the type so that callers must use `SearchResults::new`. No reviewed test enforces this. `callers_can_construct_complete_and_partial_search_results` in `tests/search.rs` does build results through `new` from outside the crate, but it never tries a struct literal, so it would still pass if `#[non_exhaustive]` were removed. `completeness_is_false_only_when_a_match_is_omitted_and_errors_propagate` runs inside the crate, where non_exhaustive has no effect. `public_exports_match_the_appendix` only compares item paths and kinds against the appendix, not attributes. A search for `SearchResults` and `compile_fail` found no compile-fail doctest for this type, though other non_exhaustive types such as `Span` have one. The attribute is therefore an obligation with no test.

text: `matches` holds the results found. `complete` is true when the search exhausted the scope. Reaching the exact limit is compatible with a complete result if no further match exists.
